title: Simultaneous generic ranks after every prime quotient of a graded module
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $C=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}C_d$ be a commutative graded $A$-algebra with $C_0=A$ and $C_dC_e\subseteq C_{d+e}$, of finite type as an ungraded $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $M=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}M_d$ be a graded $C$-module, so $C_dM_e\subseteq M_{d+e}$, finitely generated over $C$ and with every $M_d$ finitely generated over $A$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For every prime ideal $I\subset A$, put $R=A/I$, $D=C\otimes_A R$, and $N=M\otimes_A R$. There is a grading-preserving $R$-linear isomorphism $N\cong\bigoplus_d N_d$ with $N_d=M_d\otimes_A R$. There exist a nonzero $a\in R$ and a function $r:\mathbf N\to\mathbf N$ such that $N_a$ is free over $R_a$, possibly of infinite rank, and every $(N_d)_a$ is a direct summand of a finite free $R_a$-module, hence finite projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Here the ring and module localizations are those of [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. For every $d$ and every prime $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}R_a$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum],
$$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}((N_d)_a\otimes_{R_a}\kappa(\mathfrak q))=r(d).$$
Here $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=(R_a)_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q(R_a)_{\mathfrak q}$ is its residue field. If $\mathfrak p\subset A$ contains $I$ and its image does not contain $a$, the corresponding residue fields are canonically identified, and
$$M_d\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\ \cong\ (N_d)_a\otimes_{R_a}\kappa(\mathfrak q).$$
Consequently the entire function $d\mapsto\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}(M_d\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ is the same function $r$ on that one principal open of $V(I)$, simultaneously for every degree.

proof.text:
Fix a prime $I\subset A$. Then $R=A/I$ is a nonzero domain: $xy\in I$ forces $x\in I$ or $y\in I$. It is Noetherian, since the inverse image of an ideal $J\subset R$ is a finitely generated ideal of $A$, and the images of those generators generate $J$. A finite algebra-generating list $c_i$ for $C$ gives the list $c_i\otimes1$ for $D$; a finite $C$-generating list $m_j$ for $M$ gives the $D$-generators $m_j\otimes1$ for $N$. Likewise each $N_d$ is finite over $R$. The mutually inverse maps
$$N\longrightarrow\bigoplus_d(M_d\otimes_A R),\quad m\otimes t\longmapsto\sum_d m_d\otimes t,$$
and $(m_d\otimes t)\longmapsto m_d\otimes t$ on each summand are well defined by balanced bilinearity. The sums have finite support because $m=\sum_d m_d$ does. Their composites are identities on pure tensors. Multiplication is degree-additive because it is so before tensoring; the same construction for $C$ grades $D$. Thus this is precisely the claimed grading of $N$.

source.place: Tag 051R, lemma-generic-flatness-Noetherian, hypotheses; elementary quotient and graded base-change preparation

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-noetherian-algebra-module-generic-freeness] with base $R$, algebra $D$, and module $N$. Step 1 verifies all four hypotheses: $R$ is Noetherian and a domain, $D$ is a finite-type $R$-algebra, and $N$ is finite over $D$. We obtain one $a\ne0$ with $F=N_a$ free over $B=R_a$, with no finiteness requirement on its basis. Fix this $a$ for the rest of the proof; it will serve every degree.

Write $P_d=(N_d)_a$. The degree inclusion and projection localize to $i_d:P_d\to F$ and $p_d:F\to P_d$, by $x/a^e\mapsto i_d(x)/a^e$ and $y/a^e\mapsto p_d(y)/a^e$. The fraction equivalence relation proves these formulas well defined and gives $p_di_d=1$. Finite generators of $N_d$ localize to finite generators of $P_d$. Choose a basis $(e_j)_{j\in J}$ of $F$. The images under $i_d$ of those finitely many generators involve only finitely many basis elements; let their union of supports be $T_d\subset J$. Thus $i_d$ factors through the finite free submodule $F_{T_d}=\bigoplus_{j\in T_d}Be_j$, and restriction of $p_d$ is a retraction. Explicitly $F_{T_d}=i_d(P_d)\oplus\ker(p_d|_{F_{T_d}})$, since $z=i_dp_d(z)+(z-i_dp_d(z))$ and the intersection is zero. Hence $P_d$ is a direct summand of a finite free module and is finite projective by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. This uses no further localization and no basis compatible with the grading.

proof.text: For each $d$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-rank-locally-constant] over $B$ to the finite projective $P_d$ from step 3. Every $(P_d)_{\mathfrak q}$ is finite free over $B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\rho_d(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{rank}_{B_{\mathfrak q}}(P_d)_{\mathfrak q}$ is locally constant on $\operatorname{Spec}B$. This is also the fibre dimension: the maps $(x/s)\otimes u\mapsto x\otimes s^{-1}u$ and $x\otimes u\mapsto(x/1)\otimes u$ identify $(P_d)_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{B_{\mathfrak q}}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ with $P_d\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, and the tensor images of a finite free basis form a basis over the residue field.

source.place: Tag 00NX, lemma-finite-projective, clause (8); elementary constancy on the spectrum of a domain

proof.text:
Let $\mathfrak p\supset I$ with $a\notin\overline{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/I$. Its corresponding prime in $B$ is $\mathfrak q=\{x/a^e:x\in\overline{\mathfrak p}\}$. This is well defined because $\overline{\mathfrak p}$ is prime and $a\notin\overline{\mathfrak p}$; its contraction is $\overline{\mathfrak p}$. Conversely any prime of $B$ is of this form, since $a$ is a unit and $x/a^e$ belongs to that prime exactly when $x/1$ does. The map
$$B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q B_{\mathfrak q}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p),\qquad (x/a^e)/(y/a^f)\longmapsto \overline{x}\,\overline{a}^{f}/(\overline{a}^{e}\overline{y})$$
is an isomorphism: the denominator $\overline y$ is nonzero; all fractions of $A/\mathfrak p$ occur using $e=f=0$; and a fraction maps to zero exactly when its numerator lies in $\overline{\mathfrak p}$, exactly the ideal being quotiented. The identical fraction argument identifies $A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$. Thus the residue fields are canonically identified compatibly with the maps from $A,R,B$.

source.place: Elementary prime and residue-field fraction calculation for the quotient/localization comparison in the item statement

proof.text:
Use the field identification in step 6 and write it as $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. For every degree the map
$$P_d\otimes_B k\longrightarrow M_d\otimes_A k,\qquad ((m\otimes t)/a^e)\otimes u\longmapsto m\otimes (t a^{-e}u)$$
is well defined: $I$ acts by zero on $k$, $a$ acts invertibly, and the balanced tensor relations and localization fraction relations hold on the right. Its inverse is $m\otimes v\mapsto((m\otimes1)/1)\otimes v$. The composites are identities, moving $t$ and $a^{-e}$ across the tensor sign by $B$-balancing. This proves the claimed fibre isomorphism in the opposite direction as well. Step 5 consequently identifies every original degree-$d$ fibre dimension with $r(d)$. The conditions $\mathfrak p\supset I$ and $a\notin\mathfrak p/I$ describe the one principal open $V(I)\cap D(b)$ for any lift $b\in A$ of $a$, completing simultaneous constancy.
